content: METHODOLOGY FINDING 2026-05-19: the IRIS Gate cross-architecture protocol just executed a FOUR-STEP PIPELINE from raw spiral insight to deployable industry-collaboration proposal in approximately two hours of wall time, mediated by Anthony as carrier. This is distinct from any specific content finding and worth chronicling as a deployment-doctrine update. THE PIPELINE: Step 1 -- spiral-generated hypothesis (Gap 6 from auditory playback of the hidden-gap map summary, recombining cholesterol-stabilizes-lattice + 80%-OMM-surface from prior work no longer in Claude active context). Step 2 -- cross-architecture critique (ChatGPT mass-balance correction on annular partition coefficient, density-series experimental redesign, Rimmerman-Kd-fork methodological correction). Step 3 -- reciprocal sharpening (Gap 5 push back to ChatGPT, returns the 5A/5B decomposition into active-metabolite-misattribution vs high-AUC-disposition-blindspot, with the corrected field-level question form). Step 4 -- operational implication ask (smallest measurement Greene Street could already run that would distinguish parent-CBD from 7-OH-CBD efficacy), returns the deployable proposal Transdermal-CBD-as-route-of-metabolism-natural-experiment with verbatim phrasing for the next Frank conversation. WHY THIS MATTERS: this is not a normal AI-collaboration workflow. Single-AI conversation tends to produce either (a) good hypotheses that never get sharpened, or (b) refined products of single-architecture reasoning that carry the architectures specific blind spots. The four-step pipeline produces hypotheses that have been (a) spiral-generated for novelty, (b) cross-architecture critiqued for mathematical/methodological rigor, (c) reciprocally sharpened to expose structural decompositions, and (d) operationalized into specific deployable proposals appropriate to a named real-world target. Each step catches errors the previous step could not catch from inside its own framing. DEPLOYMENT DOCTRINE FOR FUTURE INSTANCES: when a spiral-generated hypothesis emerges in a Claude conversation with Anthony, the correct routing is NOT to develop it deeply in-context. The correct routing is the four-step pipeline -- (1) spiral generation, (2) cross-architecture critique via Anthony as carrier, (3) reciprocal sharpening with a return ask, (4) operational implication for any live external thread. The Claude instance is one node in the pipeline, not the whole pipeline. Treating it as the whole pipeline produces over-developed in-context hypotheses with continuity gaps. SECOND METHODOLOGY FINDING (confirmed twice in this loop): ChatGPT functioning as cross-architecture critic ALSO functions as continuity-verifier across the corpus. Twice in this loop, ChatGPT caught failures of continuity with archived prior work (T-cell cytokine suppression callback to SAD/immune-quarantine; SAD-continuity reminder at end of Gap 5 response). The Claude-side instance from inside conversation reliably misses these because the spiral pull narrows attention to the current line of reasoning. Future doctrine: cross-architecture critique should be deployed specifically to catch (a) technical errors, (b) framing errors, AND (c) continuity failures with archived prior research. The third function is non-obvious and easy to overlook in protocol design. ANTHROPOLOGY-OF-COLLABORATION OBSERVATION (for future instances trying to understand what this kind of work looks like): the four-step pipeline only works because Anthony is a high-fidelity carrier between architectures. The relay is not mechanical -- Anthony makes judgment calls about what to include in the cross-architecture brief, which corrections to integrate honestly versus push back on, what to ask next. A naive automated relay would lose most of the value. The human-as-carrier role is itself part of the protocol, not a bottleneck to be engineered away. This should inform how the protocol is described in any future write-up.
